rows.description: A teenager peppers speech with English phrases and Hindi slang to sound modern and belong to peers. Mixed talk marks the group and is also a way to express things that one language alone lacks.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager from a small town or a vernacular school is mocked for accent or English mistakes and stops speaking in class. Language can become a proxy for class, and confidence often returns with supportive peers.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult moves into polished English at an interview and into local tongue with family or drivers, sometimes using it to signal status. Awareness that language can include or exclude prevents accidental snobbery.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: In a mixed-language meeting, a speaker repeats key points in the shared language so that no one is left out. Small adjustments show respect for those less fluent.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child is taught to greet grandparents with namaste and touch their feet. Rituals of respect are learnt first as habit, and meaning grows later as affection deepens.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child asks an elder a direct question and is told not to answer back. Cultures value deference, and children still need some route to be curious and be heard.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult sits with an elder and lets the same story be told again, asking a new question each time. Elders often want to be heard and remembered more than to instruct.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult explains a phone feature or a doctor's advice slowly, without teasing, and lets the elder do the steps. Preserving an elder's dignity matters as much as the task.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult is told you do not know the world yet whenever they speak. Being unheard by someone loved is painful, and calmly asking for a real hearing can shift the pattern.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22
related mind states: affection, calm, hurt

rows.description: A caregiver speaks slowly, with a warm tone and a matching face, and the toddler responds with sounds. Very young children read tone and expression more than words.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
